call_points.text: SRB utilisation at Bharuch was 40-45% and is expected to reach 70% by August-September; CRB is lower and ramps by Q2 end and Q3.
Rail investment at Jamshedpur is due to start commercial production by calendar year-end.
Process segment grew almost 30% YoY, driven largely by wind and some metal customers, including Indian mill makers exporting.
Intercompany exports grew about 21%, led by a resilient US market; Europe is down, Australia flat, ASEAN and China down.
Plants converted from LPG to natural gas across the supply chain; beyond base oil for grease, management sees no major further cost escalation.
Manufactured versus traded mix was about 75/25, similar to earlier quarters.
The Timken GGB Technology amalgamation is with the NCLT Bangalore Bench after board approval, aimed at synergies and lower cost.
BIS certification secured for CRB, CRB rollers and TRB rollers.
Asked how much of total cost inflation had been passed through, management said it was tough to give an exact percentage; rail and PSU annual rate contracts cannot be repriced mid-term.
Asked the applicable US tariff on exports, the MD said he did not remember the exact rate.
Company is facing raw material inflation (steel, grinding wheels) and has initiated price hikes of up to **10%**.

operating_notes.text: Q4 FY26 exports stood at ₹222 crores, up significantly YoY.
Artech International filed a civil suit before the High Court of Calcutta claiming approx. ₹107.86 crore in damages challenging the termination of its distributor agreement.
Bharuch plant revenue was about ₹50 Cr in Q1FY27 and is almost at breakeven, with SRB utilisation at 40-45% and CRB lower.
Manufactured versus traded mix was about 75/25 in Q1FY27.
Steel prices rose about ₹5,000 per tonne in total (₹1,500-1,600 in January plus ₹3,500 in April), and most customers have started paying.
Q2FY27 consolidated revenue reached ₹986.04 Cr with a net profit of ₹120.90 Cr.
Timken India received two Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) licenses for Spherical Roller Bearings at its new Bharuch plant and Cylindrical Roller Bearings at its old Bharuch plant.

timeline.summary: Timken India Limited’s **Sanjay Koul** (Chairman & MD) and **Sujit Kumar Pattanaik** (CFO & WTD) to host Q4FY26 conference call on **19 May 2026 at 5:30 PM (IST)** via Avendus Spark.

On May 30, 2026, Timken India reported a civil suit filed by Artech International claiming approx. ₹107.86 crore in damages over a distributor agreement termination.

Timken India Limited will hold a Post Results Conference Call for Q2 FY 2026-27 on Friday, 30 October 2026 at 4:00 PM (IST).
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹986.04 Cr, net profit ₹120.89 Cr.
